outcome_variable_scope: Human judgements only: a rater's own stated ideal-model-behavior text against their own top/bottom ranking. No judge, no model gold head, no generated response.
scope: Length is measured in characters of the response text, and 'longer' means the rater's TOP pick is longer than their BOTTOM pick -- not longer than all four. The null is r03's C1 control (same prompt, same pair, a different person's stated text) computed within each stratum. Bootstrap clusters on annotator, as r03's own does -- r03 builds `by_ann` and resamples raters, so these intervals ARE comparable to its published one. An earlier draft of this field claimed r03 was judgement-level and therefore incomparable; that was written about code I had not read, and it survived in the artifact after being corrected in the docstring, which is the propagation failure this repository logs most often.
verdict: A AVERAGE-IS-HONEST. Entry 139 recomputed r03's verdict and surfaced a split it had never tested: the top pick is the longer response in 55.5% of judgements, and the raw hit rate splits 0.5138 against 0.4903, a gap of +0.0235 -- more than ten times r03's aggregate difference. I wrote that into three documents and tested it in none. THE STRATIFIED TEST, each stratum against ITS OWN within-stratum permuted null so that a difference in chance levels cannot masquerade as a difference in prediction: ALL n=11,327 diff +0.0017 [-0.0060,+0.0097]; top pick LONGER n=6,290 diff +0.0005 [-0.0101,+0.0111]; top pick SHORTER n=5,037 diff +0.0033 [-0.0083,+0.0148]. The difference of differences is -0.0028 [-0.0180,+0.0120], which covers zero. WHY THE RAW SPLIT AND THE TESTED GAP DIFFER: the raw split compares HIT RATES, which absorb any difference in how easy the two strata are; the tested quantity compares each stratum's hit rate to its OWN permuted null, which is the only version that isolates prediction. BOOTSTRAP IS CLUSTERED ON ANNOTATOR (1,001 raters, 11,327 judgements) and both strata are recomputed inside each draw so the arms stay paired. This round reproduces r03's aggregate to 3e-17 on the difference before any stratum is read -- a control it did not have until its first version returned an aggregate hit rate of 0.1943 against r03's 0.5033, because it scored ties as misses where r03 scores them 0.5.
